name: scorbit-sdk
$comment-purpose: The SDK has been buildable on Windows with vcpkg for about a year, but only
from a configuration that lived in one person's shell history. Nothing in the
repository described it, so no CI could run it and no second machine could
reproduce it. This file is that configuration, committed.
It is inert on Linux and macOS: vcpkg reads it only when CMake is invoked with
vcpkg's toolchain file, which nothing outside the Windows job does. Where it
does apply, find_package for Boost, CURL, LibArchive and OpenSSL is satisfied
from vcpkg, so the CPM fallbacks in cmake/lib_*.cmake never trigger.
No version field on purpose. VERSION is the single source of truth for the
SDK's version and CMakeLists.txt reads it from there; repeating it here would
create a second copy to drift. vcpkg does not require one for a manifest that
$comment-triplet: MultiThreaded$<$<CONFIG:Debug>:Debug>DLL -- the dynamic CRT. The -md triplet
is static libraries against that dynamic runtime. Plain x64-windows-static
uses the static CRT instead and mismatches, and the resulting LNK2038 errors
read nothing like a triplet problem.
$comment-dependencies: Derived from the source tree, not iterated out of a failing build. The boost
entries are the union of three readings:
1. CMakeLists.txt BOOST_COMPILED_COMPONENTS + BOOST_HEADER_ONLY_COMPONENTS
2. tests/test_detail/CMakeLists.txt -- identical sets to the root, so it
contributes nothing, but it is checked so that a future divergence does
3. a sweep of #include <boost/...> across source/, libs/ and centrifugo-cpp
Only the sweep contributes boost-predef and boost-system, and both are
genuinely reached rather than transitively satisfied: predef in updater.cpp,
utils/mac_address.cpp and utils/machine_fingerprint.cpp; system in
utils/lan_ip.cpp. Neither is declared to find_package anywhere.
A component used but not declared is exactly what broke this build before.
boost-url was absent from the original port list, so find_package(Boost ...
url) failed, lib_boost.cmake fell back to CPM, and CPM's boost collided with
vcpkg's already-defined targets in roughly forty ALIAS errors. The collision
was the symptom; the missing port was the cause.
So: when a new boost header starts being included, add its port here. Keep
this list derived from the tree rather than grown one CI failure at a time.
boost-json and boost-program-options were in the original configuration and
are deliberately absent now -- nothing in the tree includes <boost/json/...>
or <boost/program_options/...> any more.
$comment-baseline: builtin-baseline pins the vcpkg registry commit, so the same port versions
resolve on every machine. Without it each host builds against whatever its
own vcpkg clone happens to be at, which is the class of problem this file
exists to end. Bump it deliberately, not incidentally.
